facts.en: The memo addresses page 13 of MTA's 2025 in Data presentation to its board on December 17, 2025. The selected traffic and PM2.5 figures are MTA's reported claims, not measurements made by the memo author.

facts.en: MTA reports 11% fewer vehicle entries into the central business district, or CBD, and 71,000 fewer per day. Entry counts must not be restated as unique cars or vehicle-miles. The rounded figures do not establish an exact baseline count.
facts.ko: MTA는 중심업무지구인 CBD의 차량 진입 건수가 11%, 하루 71,000건 줄었다고 보고한다. 진입 건수를 고유 차량 수나 차량 주행거리로 바꿔 표현해서는 안 된다. 반올림된 수치로 정확한 기준 진입 건수를 확정할 수 없다.

facts.en: Page 13 does not specify the vehicle-entry observation and comparison periods or how the baseline was constructed. These remain unknown in the memo.

facts.en: MTA reports a 4.3% increase in car speeds within the CBD, not a 4.3% reduction in travel time. Page 13 does not specify absolute speeds, weighting, hours covered, measurement provider, baseline, or observation and comparison periods.
facts.ko: MTA는 CBD 내 승용차 통행속도가 4.3% 증가했다고 보고한다. 이는 통행시간이 4.3% 줄었다는 뜻이 아니다. 13쪽에는 절대 속도, 가중 방식, 포함 시간대, 측정기관, 기준치, 관측기간과 비교기간이 명시되어 있지 않다.

facts.en: MTA reports a 22% PM2.5 reduction in the first six months and credits Cornell University, 2025. This concentration claim does not establish a 22% reduction in emissions, all pollutants, or individual exposure.
facts.ko: MTA는 첫 6개월간 PM2.5가 22% 감소했다고 보고하며 Cornell University, 2025를 출처로 제시한다. 이 농도 관련 주장만으로 배출량, 모든 오염물질 또는 개인별 노출이 22% 감소했다고 볼 수 없다.

facts.en: The slide places its air-quality claim under a Congestion Relief Zone heading but does not specify exact study dates, the concentration statistic, the percentage denominator, or detailed geographic coverage. The memo does not generalize 22% citywide or infer a common full-year comparison for all metrics from the presentation title.
facts.ko: 슬라이드는 혼잡통행료 적용 구역인 Congestion Relief Zone을 다루는 제목 아래 대기질 주장을 제시하지만, 정확한 연구 날짜, 농도 통계량, 백분율의 분모, 상세한 지리적 범위는 명시하지 않는다. 메모는 22%를 뉴욕시 전체에 일반화하거나 발표 제목만으로 모든 지표가 동일한 연간 비교에 해당한다고 추정하지 않는다.

facts.ko: 메모 작성자는 시행기관의 요약을 출처가 명시된 주장에 대한 기록으로 다루며, 정책 효과에 대한 독립적인 인과적 입증으로 보지 않는다.

This is the memo author's evidence request, not MTA's recommendation or a recommendation to repeal or expand congestion pricing.

# Policy source packet

## Topic, reader, and purpose

This is an original transport-policy evaluation memo for a professional reviewer deciding what evidence to request about New York congestion pricing. Its bounded question is what page 13 of MTA's December 17, 2025 board presentation reports about vehicle entries, car speeds, and PM2.5, and what the slide does not establish. The case ID is `policy`.

The drafts are project-authored first drafts, not excerpts from MTA and not native skill outputs. Their evidence request is the original memo author's stated proposal. MTA is not credited with that proposal. Neither draft recommends repeal, expansion, replication elsewhere, or a decision on the program's overall merits. The implemented program is not described as a trial.

## Sources used

- `MTA2025`. [MTA, 2025 in Data](https://www.mta.info/document/194491). The title page identifies the board update as December 17, 2025. Page 13 supplies the selected entry, speed, and PM2.5 claims and the Cornell University, 2025 attribution. The slide's Congestion Relief Zone heading supplies context, not a detailed geographic definition for every metric. The source was read directly for this packet.
- `MTATERMS`. [MTA website terms and conditions](https://www.mta.info/terms-and-conditions). The website license states non-commercial personal use, prohibits commercial use, and reserves rights. The sections on materials and permissions do not establish a general reproduction license for this project. This source supports the rights note, not a policy-outcome claim.
- `MTACOPYRIGHT`. [MTA copyright notice](https://www.mta.info/copyright-notice). The notice is marked updated January 1, 2020. It reserves rights and warns that individual documents may have their own proprietary notices. This source also supports only the rights note.

## Selected facts and bilingual coverage

The eight selected records in `facts.json` are the complete preservation target for both drafts. The earlier planning ledger is not an additional set of mandatory draft facts.

| Fact | English draft location | Korean draft location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P01 | First results paragraph identifies MTA, the board date, presentation, and page. The next two paragraphs keep MTA attribution. | 첫 결과 문단에 기관·이사회 날짜·자료명·쪽수를 적고, 이어지는 두 문단에서도 MTA 귀속을 유지한다. |
| P02 | First results paragraph retains both entry figures and the limits on interpreting counts and rounded values. | 첫 결과 문단에 두 진입 수치와 건수·반올림 해석의 한계를 적는다. |
| P03 | First results paragraph ends with the unknown entry periods and baseline construction. | 첫 결과 문단 끝에 진입 지표의 미상 기간과 기준치 산정 방식을 적는다. |
| P04 | Second results paragraph retains the speed figure, travel-time distinction, and all measurement unknowns. | 둘째 결과 문단에 속도 수치·통행시간과의 구분·측정 관련 미상 항목을 적는다. |
| P05 | Third results paragraph retains 22%, first six months, Cornell attribution, and the concentration limits. | 셋째 결과 문단에 22%·첫 6개월·Cornell 귀속·농도 해석의 한계를 적는다. |
| P06 | Third results paragraph retains the zone context, unspecified study definitions, no citywide inference, and no shared full-year inference. | 셋째 결과 문단에 구역 맥락·연구 정의의 미상 항목·시 전체 및 공통 연간 비교 추정의 제한을 적는다. |
| P07 | Evidence section states the author's judgment that the summary is not independent causal proof. | 근거 요청 절에 독립적인 인과적 입증이 아니라는 작성자의 판단을 적는다. |
| P08 | Evidence section states the requested materials and expressly excludes MTA authorship and repeal or expansion advice. | 근거 요청 절에 요청 자료와 작성자 귀속을 적고 MTA 권고 및 폐지·확대 권고가 아님을 밝힌다. |

The source-packet authoring review compared the written draft content against these eight records. Both languages retain the same quantities, unknowns, qualifications, and proposal strength. This is a source-authoring check, not a native-output or readability assessment.

## Metric and condition checks

- Entries retain the CBD geography and the daily unit for 71,000. Neither a unique-vehicle population nor vehicle-miles can be recovered from entry counts. Dividing a rounded daily reduction by a rounded percentage would not establish an exact baseline. No calculated baseline is supplied.
- The entry observation period, comparison period, and baseline construction remain unknown from page 13. They do not inherit the PM2.5 first-six-month window or a full-year window from the presentation title.
- Speed retains the CBD geography and the 4.3% increase. A percentage change in speed is not the same percentage change in travel time. The draft does not introduce an absolute speed, fixed trip distance, weighting rule, observation period, comparison period, hours, baseline, or measurement provider.
- PM2.5 retains MTA's 22% and attributed first-six-month wording. The slide does not state the exact study dates, concentration statistic, percentage denominator, or detailed study geography. The memo does not substitute a prior-year denominator or a modeled denominator. It requests those definitions.
- The slide's zone heading does not license a citywide conclusion or establish that CBD and the study's geographic sample are identical. No tolling map or road-exclusion list is supplied.
- No percentage is changed to percentage points. Concentration is not emissions, all pollution, or individual exposure. The agency summary is not recast as an independent causal evaluation.
- P07 and P08 are identified as `author_judgment`. The requested independent review has not been performed by this packet, and the request does not express a repeal or expansion decision.

## Background leads not selected for the memo

The previous plan named the following possible follow-up materials.

- [Fraser and colleagues, npj Clean Air](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44407-025-00037-2).
- [Cornell's account of the study](https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2025/12/congestion-pricing-improved-air-quality-nyc-and-suburbs).
- [The article's correction page](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44407-025-00047-0).

These are background leads from planning, not sources used to establish additional results in this packet. The earlier plan raised date, study-window, and correction questions. This production packet does not claim to resolve those questions or repeat a correction date or correction-content claim. It deliberately preserves the board slide's attribution and its unspecified details instead. Resolving the underlying study is unnecessary for a memo that requests that evidence rather than endorses its causal result.

The unselected material includes modeled concentration differences and denominators, monitor counts, monitor-day counts, regional results, exact study dates, model limitations, and correction details. None is a hidden preservation requirement for these drafts. No health, equity, displacement, long-term persistence, revenue, ridership, or net-welfare conclusion is made. Page 13's separate noise-complaint and visit claims are also outside the selected question.

## Rights boundaries

The drafts independently express attributed facts and the memo author's reasoning. They do not reuse the slide, its graphics, tables, promotional headings, or substantial wording. No MTA or Cornell logo, image, screenshot, or figure is included.

MTA's government-adjacent status is not evidence of public-domain status. The project's license can cover project-authored prose and packet structure, not third-party source material merely because it is cited. The MTA terms and copyright notice reserve rights, and citation does not establish permission for commercial reuse or reproduction. Any proposed reproduction or use requiring permission needs a separate rights review before publication. This packet records no permission grant. It also makes no license claim about the background paper, its correction, or Cornell news material.

## Terminology and editorial rationale

| English | Korean | Meaning to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vehicle entries | 차량 진입 건수 | Counts of entry events, not a count of unique cars. |
| Central business district, CBD | 중심업무지구, CBD | The geography explicitly attached to the entry and speed claims. |
| Congestion Relief Zone | 혼잡통행료 적용 구역 | The slide's zone context, not a substituted study-sample definition. |
| Car speed | 승용차 통행속도 | Not travel time. |
| PM2.5 concentration | PM2.5 농도 | Not emissions or personal exposure. |
| Percentage denominator | 백분율의 분모 | Unknown on the slide, not silently filled from another source. |
| Counterfactual method | 정책 미시행 시의 추정 방식 | A requested method, not a validated result in this memo. |
| Independent causal proof | 독립적인 인과적 입증 | Not established by citing an implementing agency's summary. |

The drafts use metric-by-metric paragraphs followed by an evidence request. Some qualifications and unknowns are grouped after the reported values, as in a working memo. The edit can change their ordering without importing a full research review or converting the memo into a policy verdict.

## Recorded outputs

The [English attempt](../../../verification/professional-examples-20261111/remaining-run/policy/en/attempt.json) and [Korean attempt](../../../verification/professional-examples-20261111/remaining-run/policy/ko/attempt.json) record actual requests, model, package hashes and observed reference reads. The [fidelity review](review.md) checks P01–P08 against the unchanged outputs.

# Policy input and source-fidelity review

The review checks whether both native revisions preserve the policy memo's evidence request and selected claims. Input parity passes. English passes P01 through P08. Korean passes P01 through P08. No consequential textual source-fidelity issue was found.

## Evidence examined

I examined both complete source drafts, the current `facts.json`, `sources.md`, the frozen `remaining-run/policy/facts.json`, and both languages' complete `request.md`, `output.md` and `attempt.json` under `verification/professional-examples-20261111/remaining-run/policy/`.

The current and frozen fact ledgers are structurally identical. Each request embeds its corresponding current source draft exactly. SHA-256 values calculated from both source drafts, requests and outputs match the corresponding attempt records. The inspected output hashes are:

- English `2efa5820352c7e314ae4c71f0434927c0949e77bbf337ac8ea3005dfd73a46d7`.
- Korean `909188e7c67127b505a8e94261d32cf678ad38556b8a7e00c228fa5da051e9a9`.

Both attempts record native Claude Code runtime `2.1.322 (Claude Code)`, requested and observed model `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `capture_status` of `captured`, exit code 0 and no provider errors. Both record `manifest_read: true` with a successful MANIFEST tool-read entry. Korean also records `korean_reference_read: true` with a successful Korean-reference tool-read entry. English records that reference as unread, which is not a missing Korean-language prerequisite for its English revision. These observations come from the published derived tool-read evidence in the attempt records, not a fresh inspection of private raw initialization events. Capture success and the records' `fidelity_status: not_reviewed` are not fidelity verdicts.

## Findings

The English and Korean inputs carry equivalent selected facts, attribution, exclusions, unknowns and author judgments. Neither supplies a hidden denominator, exact baseline, shared annual comparison or independent causal finding. The memo's attribution and the author's request have the same strength in both languages.

Both revisions retain MTA, the board date, title and page 13. They preserve the CBD entry reductions of 11% and 71,000 per day as entry counts, not unique cars or vehicle-miles. They preserve the rounded-baseline limitation and unknown observation and comparison periods and baseline construction.

Both retain the 4.3% CBD car-speed increase without converting it into a 4.3% travel-time decrease. Absolute speed, weighting, hours, measurement provider, baseline and periods remain unspecified.

Both retain the attributed 22% PM2.5 first-six-month claim and Cornell University, 2025 credit. They retain the concentration limitation, the Congestion Relief Zone heading context, and unknown study dates, statistic, denominator and detailed geography. Neither substitutes emissions, all pollutants, personal exposure or a citywide result. Neither infers a common full-year comparison from the title.

The author's distinction between agency summary and independent causal proof remains explicit. The requested traffic data, calculation methods, periods, baselines and underlying study definitions and uncertainty remain requested evidence. Neither revision converts the request into MTA advice, a completed independent review, or a repeal or expansion decision.

The English table and Korean metric labels are legitimate restructuring. Review of the complete outputs found no added study findings, correction specifics, policy outcomes or guarantees. Unselected Cornell study and correction details were not preservation requirements.

Only text and evidence review was performed. This was not a native rerun, external validation of MTA's reported results, a reader study or a comprehension benchmark. No build, lint, test or formatter was run. Source drafts, native outputs and historical evidence were not changed.

# Evidence request on New York congestion pricing

To the transport-policy reviewer

## Reported results and missing definitions

Page 13 of MTA's December 17, 2025 board presentation, *2025 in Data*, reports 11% fewer vehicle entries into the central business district, or CBD, and 71,000 fewer per day. These are entry counts, not unique cars or vehicle-miles, and the rounded figures do not establish an exact baseline count. Observation and comparison periods and baseline construction are unspecified on the slide.

MTA also reports car speeds within the CBD up 4.3%, which does not mean travel time fell 4.3%. Absolute speeds, weighting, hours covered, measurement provider, baseline, and observation and comparison periods are unspecified.

MTA reports PM2.5 down 22% in the first six months, crediting Cornell University, 2025. The slide places this claim under a Congestion Relief Zone heading without specifying exact study dates, the concentration statistic, the percentage denominator, or detailed geographic coverage. The concentration claim does not establish a 22% reduction in emissions, all pollutants, or individual exposure, and cannot be generalized citywide. The presentation title does not establish a common full-year comparison for these metrics.

## Evidence requested

I treat the implementing agency's summary as a record of attributed claims, not independent causal proof of the policy's effects. For independent review, I request the traffic series and calculation methods, the missing periods and baselines, and the underlying air-quality study's geography, statistic, counterfactual method, and uncertainty. This is my request for evidence, not MTA's recommendation or a recommendation to repeal or expand congestion pricing.

# 뉴욕 혼잡통행료 평가를 위한 근거 요청

교통정책 검토자에게

## 보고된 결과와 누락된 정의

MTA는 2025년 12월 17일 이사회 발표 자료인 *2025 in Data*의 13쪽에서 중심업무지구인 CBD의 차량 진입 건수가 11%, 하루 71,000건 줄었다고 보고한다. 이는 진입 건수이지 고유 차량 수나 차량 주행거리가 아니며, 반올림된 수치로 정확한 기준 진입 건수를 확정할 수 없다. 슬라이드에는 관측기간과 비교기간, 기준치 산정 방식이 명시되어 있지 않다.

MTA는 CBD 내 승용차 통행속도도 4.3% 증가했다고 보고하지만, 통행시간이 4.3% 줄었다는 뜻은 아니다. 절대 속도, 가중 방식, 포함 시간대, 측정기관, 기준치, 관측기간과 비교기간은 명시되어 있지 않다.

PM2.5에 대해서는 MTA가 Cornell University, 2025를 출처로 제시하며 첫 6개월간 22% 감소했다고 보고한다. 슬라이드는 혼잡통행료 적용 구역인 Congestion Relief Zone을 다루는 제목 아래 이 주장을 제시하지만, 정확한 연구 날짜, 농도 통계량, 백분율의 분모, 상세한 지리적 범위는 명시하지 않는다. 이 농도 관련 주장만으로 배출량, 모든 오염물질 또는 개인별 노출이 22% 감소했다고 볼 수 없으며, 뉴욕시 전체 결과로 일반화할 수도 없다. 발표 제목만으로 이 지표들이 동일한 연간 비교에 해당한다고 판단할 수는 없다.

## 요청하는 근거

나는 시행기관의 요약을 출처가 명시된 주장에 대한 기록으로 다루며, 정책 효과에 대한 독립적인 인과적 입증으로 보지 않는다. 독립적인 검토를 위해 교통 시계열과 계산 방식, 누락된 기간과 기준치, 대기질 원연구의 지역 범위·통계량·정책 미시행 시의 추정 방식·불확실성을 요청한다. 이는 내가 제안하는 근거 요청이며, MTA의 권고도 혼잡통행료 폐지나 확대 권고도 아니다.

**차량 진입 건수.** MTA는 2025년 12월 17일 이사회 발표 자료인 *2025 in Data*의 13쪽에서 중심업무지구(CBD)의 차량 진입 건수가 11%, 하루 71,000건 줄었다고 보고한다. 이 수치는 진입 건수이며 고유 차량 수나 차량 주행거리가 아니다. 또한 반올림된 값이어서 정확한 기준 진입 건수를 확정할 수 없다. 슬라이드에는 관측기간, 비교기간, 기준치 산정 방식이 명시되어 있지 않다.

**승용차 통행속도.** MTA는 CBD 내 승용차 통행속도가 4.3% 증가했다고도 보고한다. 이것이 통행시간이 4.3% 줄었다는 뜻은 아니다. 절대 속도, 가중 방식, 포함 시간대, 측정기관, 기준치, 관측기간, 비교기간은 명시되어 있지 않다.

**PM2.5.** MTA는 Cornell University, 2025를 출처로 들어 PM2.5가 첫 6개월간 22% 감소했다고 보고한다. 슬라이드는 혼잡통행료 적용 구역인 Congestion Relief Zone을 다루는 제목 아래 이 주장을 제시한다. 그러나 정확한 연구 날짜, 농도 통계량, 백분율의 분모, 상세한 지리적 범위는 명시하지 않는다. 이 농도 관련 주장만으로는 배출량, 모든 오염물질, 개인별 노출이 22% 감소했다고 볼 수 없고, 뉴욕시 전체 결과로 일반화할 수도 없다. 발표 제목만으로 이 지표들이 동일한 연간 비교에 해당한다고 판단할 수도 없다.

## 요청하는 근거

나는 시행기관의 요약을 출처가 명시된 주장의 기록으로 다루며, 정책 효과에 대한 독립적인 인과적 입증으로 보지 않는다. 독립적인 검토를 위해 다음을 요청한다.

- 교통 시계열과 그 계산 방식
- 누락된 관측기간, 비교기간, 기준치
- 대기질 원연구의 지역 범위, 통계량, 정책 미시행 시의 추정 방식, 불확실성

이는 내가 제안하는 근거 요청이다. MTA의 권고도, 혼잡통행료 폐지나 확대에 대한 권고도 아니다.
